newsitem.title: CANADA: Top Canada inspector sees fusarium on 2 pct wheat.
newsitem.headline: Top Canada inspector sees fusarium on 2 pct wheat.

text.p: Two percent of the top grades of western Canadian milling wheat are infected with fusarium head blight, the Canadian Grain Commission's chief grain inspector said.
"We've looked at 5,000 samples so far and fusarium in the top grades is running at two percent," CGC chief grain inspector Len Seguin told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Fusarium (scab) struck Manitoba's Red River Valley and spread northwest to Dauphin and into bordering crop districts of eastern Saskatchewan in July.
The fungus is brought on by prolonged rain during heading and can produce vomitoxin, which in high levels can cause nausea.
Grain standards are set in November by a farmer and industry committee based on 25,000 samples tested by the CGC.
Submission of samples from Prairie farmers has been delayed by rain and snow during the harvest, Seguin said.
"We certainly have a whole array of grading factors this year," Seguin said.
There are anecdotal reports of bleaching and sprouting from the wet harvest in the west and frost damage to some swathed crops.
"Ergot is certainly going to be a big factor but more in Saskatchewan than Manitoba," Seguin added.
Ergot is a fungus that strikes cereals in the flowering stage.
